words.definition: The feeling of being completely full or gratified after having enough of something.
words.example: After the third helping of pie, a heavy satiety set in and he could not eat another bite.
words.mnemonic: Root 'sate' (to fill fully) + -iety — the state of being sated.

words.definition: An abnormal or ugly growth protruding from a body or surface.
words.example: A knotty excrescence bulged from the old oak's trunk like a fist of tangled wood.
words.mnemonic: Latin 'crescere' = to grow (as in crescendo) — an unwanted thing that grew out.

words.definition: Far exceeding what is reasonable or customary, especially in price or amount.
words.example: The tiny hotel room cost an exorbitant sum that drained half our vacation budget.
words.mnemonic: Ex + orbit — a price so high it flies out of orbit.

words.definition: Going beyond sensible limits; excessive in degree or amount.
words.example: His immoderate spending left the account empty long before the month was over.
words.mnemonic: im- (not) + moderate — literally 'not moderate'.

words.definition: Showing a lack of self-control, especially in drinking or heated behavior.
words.example: His intemperate outburst at the meeting embarrassed everyone and cost him the promotion.
words.mnemonic: in- (not) + temper — can't keep your temper in check.

words.definition: The practice of deliberately choosing not to indulge in something, such as food or alcohol.
words.example: During Lent she kept a strict abstinence from sweets, sugar, and rich desserts.
words.mnemonic: abs-tighten: hold your abs tight and resist the snack.

words.definition: Self-control, or the act of holding back an impulse or action.
words.example: It took great restraint not to reply to the insulting email while he was still angry.
words.mnemonic: re-STRAIN — like a leash straining to hold something back.

words.definition: The ability to control one's impulses or bodily functions.
words.example: The monk's remarkable continence let him refuse every luxury offered to him.
words.mnemonic: Sounds like 'contain' — you keep everything contained within yourself.

words.definition: Unable to control natural bodily functions, or lacking self-restraint.
words.example: So incontinent were his desires that he bought every gadget he laid eyes on.
words.mnemonic: in- (not) + contain — can't contain it.

words.definition: Behaving in a sexually unrestrained and morally unprincipled way.
words.example: The novel scandalized readers with its licentious characters and their nightly escapades.
words.mnemonic: Like 'license' — acting as if granted a license to break every moral rule.

words.definition: Excessive indulgence in sensual pleasures such as drinking and sex.
words.example: The weekend of debauchery left the mansion trashed and every guest hungover for days.
words.mnemonic: Sounds like 'the-bawdy' — a scene of bawdy, sinful excess.

words.definition: Done deliberately and maliciously without reason, or lacking moral restraint.
words.example: The vandals smashed the windows in a fit of wanton destruction, for no reason at all.
words.mnemonic: Sounds like 'want-on' — always wanting on and on with no limits.

words.definition: Not held back or controlled; completely free of limits.
words.example: Her unbridled enthusiasm swept the whole room into cheering along with her.
words.mnemonic: un + bridle — a horse with no bridle, running wild.

words.definition: Showing excessive pride, confidence, or arrogance.
words.example: His overweening certainty that he would win made his eventual loss all the more humiliating.
words.mnemonic: Sounds like 'over-winning' — someone sure he's always winning.

words.definition: Far greater than what is usual, expected, or reasonable.
words.example: She spent an inordinate amount of time choosing a font for a one-page flyer.
words.mnemonic: in- (not) + ordinary — an amount that is beyond ordinary.

words.definition: The habit of eating and drinking far more than one actually needs.
words.example: By his third helping of pie, his gluttony had drawn stares from the other guests.
words.mnemonic: Sounds like 'glut' — a glut is an oversupply, and this is oversupplying yourself with food.

words.definition: Extremely hungry, to the point of wanting to eat right away.
words.example: After the twelve-hour hike, the campers fell on their supper like ravenous wolves.
words.mnemonic: A raven scavenging for scraps is always on the hunt — picture that bird, endlessly hungry.

words.definition: To eat greedily and in very large quantities.
words.example: The children gormandized their way through the entire tray of cupcakes in minutes.
words.mnemonic: Hidden inside is 'gourmand' — a gourmand who loses all restraint does this at the table.

words.definition: The belief that seeking pleasure is the most important thing in life.
words.example: His weekend of nonstop parties and indulgence was hedonism at its purest.
words.mnemonic: From Greek 'hedone' (pleasure); picture a permanent 'heyday' of fun with no other goal.

words.definition: Devoted to seeking enjoyment and comfort above all else.
words.example: The resort catered to a hedonistic crowd chasing sun, cocktails, and midnight dancing.
words.mnemonic: Same Greek root 'hedone' (pleasure) — a 'hey-day' lifestyle turned into an adjective.

words.definition: A person who loves luxury, comfort, and sensual pleasure.
words.example: A true sybarite, she wouldn't travel unless the hotel had silk sheets and a private chef.
words.mnemonic: From Sybaris, an ancient Greek city whose citizens were famous for extravagant, pampered living.

words.definition: Fond of and devoted to fine food, drink, and refined pleasures.
words.example: The epicurean menu paired each course with a rare vintage from the cellar.
words.mnemonic: Named for philosopher Epicurus; hear 'epic cuisine' and picture a magnificent meal.

words.definition: Someone whose life centers on luxury and sensual gratification.
words.example: The aging voluptuary surrounded himself with velvet cushions, fine wine, and soft music.
words.mnemonic: It contains 'voluptuous' — this is the person who chases every voluptuous, sensual delight.

words.definition: Involving wild, drunken celebration and uncontrolled merrymaking.
words.example: The graduation party turned bacchanalian, with people dancing on tables until dawn.
words.mnemonic: From Bacchus, the Roman god of wine, whose festivals were riotous drinking parties.

words.definition: Marked by wild, unrestrained indulgence in pleasure or excess.
words.example: The festival's orgiastic frenzy of music, food, and dance lasted three full nights.
words.mnemonic: Built on 'orgy' — an orgy is unbridled excess, and this word describes that frenzy.

words.definition: The state of being full of energy, excitement, and cheerfulness.
words.example: The puppy's exuberance sent it bounding around the yard, unable to sit still.
words.mnemonic: 'Ex-' (out) + Latin 'uber' (abundant) — abundance bursting outward.

words.definition: To speak or write about something at great length and in detail.
words.example: Given any chance, the professor would expatiate on medieval trade routes for a solid hour.
words.mnemonic: 'Ex-' (out) + Latin 'spatium' (space) — to roam out over a wide space of words.

words.definition: A small or moderate amount of something.
words.example: If you had a modicum of sense, you'd bring an umbrella on a day like this.
words.mnemonic: Sounds like 'modest' plus 'cup' — just a modest cupful, only a little.

words.definition: A small, superficial amount, especially of knowledge.
words.example: He knew only a smattering of French, enough to order coffee and little else.
words.mnemonic: Think 'scatter' — a few bits scattered thinly, never a full grasp.

words.definition: A tiny trace or spark of something.
words.example: There wasn't a scintilla of evidence linking her to the crime.
words.mnemonic: Related to 'scintillate' (to sparkle) — this is a single, tiny spark.

words.definition: The state of having far more of something than is needed or wanted.
words.example: The nimiety of gifts under the tree left the children overwhelmed rather than delighted.
words.mnemonic: From Latin 'nimis' meaning too much — a nimiety is simply too many.

words.definition: Having a dashing, jaunty, and slightly disreputable stylish air.
words.example: He wore his hat at a rakish angle, a cigarette dangling with careless confidence.
words.mnemonic: A 'rake' was an old word for a fashionable scoundrel — rakish is his jaunty swagger.

words.definition: To drink alcohol and celebrate in a noisy, lively manner.
words.example: The sailors caroused in the tavern until dawn, draining tankard after tankard.
words.mnemonic: Sounds like 'car rouse' — rowdy drinkers rousing the whole street.

words.definition: Noisy, lively celebration full of dancing, laughter, and merrymaking.
words.example: The wedding revelry spilled into the garden, lasting well past midnight.
words.mnemonic: Picture people who 'rebel' against calm — revelry is joyful rebellion against quiet.

words.definition: A person who enjoys eating and often consumes food in large amounts.
words.example: A true gourmand, he ordered three courses and finished every plate without hesitation.
words.mnemonic: Sounds like 'gorge' plus 'demand' — someone who demands to gorge.

words.definition: Swollen or bulging; also describing inflated, pompous speech.
words.example: His ankle grew tumid after the fall, straining against his shoelaces.
words.mnemonic: Sounds like 'tummy' that's swollen — a tumid belly bulges outward.

words.definition: Sedate, respectable, and unadventurous in manner or character.
words.example: The staid old banker frowned at the boisterous crowd outside his office.
words.mnemonic: Sounds like 'stayed' — someone who stayed put, settled and calm, never wild.

words.definition: A state of moral or cultural decline marked by excessive self-indulgence.
words.example: The empire's final years were steeped in decadence: lavish feasts and idle luxury.
words.mnemonic: Shares its root with 'decay' — picture a society decaying through too much luxury.

words.definition: Readily affected by or giving pleasure to the body rather than the mind.
words.example: The sensuous music, warm candlelight, and scent of jasmine filled the room with delight.
words.mnemonic: Contains 'sense' — it is all about pleasing what the body can feel.

words.definition: Existing in an extremely large or more than ample quantity.
words.example: After the rains, the valley yielded superabundant crops, more than the villagers could store.
words.mnemonic: 'Super' piled onto 'abundant' — plenty taken over the top.

words.definition: Not affected by alcohol; also serious, calm, and restrained in manner.
words.example: After the chaos of the party, she stayed sober and drove her tipsy friends home.
words.mnemonic: Break it as 'so bare' — a clear, bare mind untouched by drink.

words.definition: Kept within reasonable limits; not extreme, excessive, or intense.
words.example: She kept a moderate pace on the hike, neither rushing ahead nor lagging behind.
words.mnemonic: Shares a root with 'modest' and 'mode' — holding to a modest middle.

words.definition: To satisfy or quench a thirst, craving, or desire.
words.example: A tall glass of cold water finally slaked his thirst after the long desert trek.
words.mnemonic: Sounds like 'lake' — drink from a lake to slake your thirst.

description: advanced and low-frequency — excess and moderation
